newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission proposes phasing out Nordic alcohol limits.
newsitem.headline: Commission proposes phasing out Nordic alcohol limits.

text.p: The European Commission proposed a directive on Wednesday to require Denmark, Finland and Sweden to phase out their limits on the amount of alcohol and tobacco products that travellers bring home by June 30, 2002.

"I am ready to take account of the difficulties of the Nordic countries by giving them a transition period to adopt their social and health protection policies," European Union Internal Market Commissioner Mario Monti said in a statement.

However, he said the quotas must end because they violate a fundamental principle of the EU's single market -- the right of citizens to carry goods for their personal use freely across borders within the EU.

The question is a sensitive one for the Nordic states, which have traditionally applied high taxes on alcohol and tobacco to discourage consumption and raise revenue. They apply those taxes to products brought in from other EU countries above certain limits, thus keeping out cheaper imports.
Sweden has said that it cannot accept any deadline for ending the restrictions.

The Commission said it had proposed that the three countries immediately reduce the minimum period that travellers must be away to qualify for tax exemptions on alcohol and tobacco from 36 hours to 24 hours.
Directive 92/12/EEC gives Denmark, Finland and Sweden a derogation to EU law for tobacco and alcohol imports until December 31, 1996.
